title: Customer requests synthesis — clustered themes & quick wins (Jul 2025)
content:
Executive summary:

This note synthesizes direct customer conversations, support tickets, and AE input collected in June–early July 2025 (N ≈ 48 accounts; mix of mid-market and enterprise). Goal: surface clustered themes, quantify incidence, provide representative verbatims, and recommend immediate/near-term actions (0–3 months) and longer roadmap asks (3–9 months).

High-level takeaways:
- Top customer pain: unpredictable tail latency under bursty traffic patterns leading to user-facing errors or timeouts. Reported by ~40% of accounts (esp. those on Dedicated).
- High-value feature asks: (1) better per-request routing controls (region/cost/latency), (2) ability to pin model variant + auto-fallback policies, (3) richer observability for per-token costs and latency attribution, (4) easier private deployment onboarding (VPC templates + checklist).
- Quick wins available: improve documentation for autoscaling config, add a canned policy template for canary -> fallback, and ship a one-click KV-prefix cache toggle in console.

Methodology and sources:
- Sources: AE meeting notes (12 calls), Support tickets tagged "latency"/"fallback" (34 tickets), latest CS feedback workshop 2025-07-01, and product experiments log.
- Accounts sampled: 48 (24 SMB/prosumer, 20 mid-market, 4 enterprise). Weighted by ARR for impact scoring.
- Coding of asks: open-coding, then affinity cluster into 7 themes.

Clustered themes (ordered by weighted impact score):

1) Tail latency & burst handling (weight: high) — reported by 19 accounts
Representative verbatims:
- "We see 95th->99th spike during marketing bursts, kills our page load SLA."
- "Autoscaler scales too slow for sudden bursts and we hit timeouts; we need a cheaper burst buffer tier."

Problem breakdown:
- Autoscaling reaction time vs. request queueing.
- Lack of a low-cost burst capacity that can be used for short windows.
- Insufficient visibility on per-request queue depth and fallback counts.

Suggested immediate actions (0–3 months):
- Add a troubleshooting doc + checklist for Dedicated autoscale tuning (docs owner: eng-console, priority: P1).
- Expose a temporary "burst mode" config in Console (toggle default off) that routes to pre-warmed pool for N minutes. (PM prototyping: product-hosted-api).

Longer term (3–9 months):
- Implement a tiered capacity offering or fast-warm function that can be billed differently and integrated with routing policies. (Cross-team: serving-runtime + dedicated).

2) Observability: per-route/per-token cost attribution & sample tracing (weight: high) — reported by 14 accounts
Representative verbatims:
- "We cannot reconcile our bill to user sessions — need token-level mapping in logs."
- "If we had token heatmaps per-prompt type we could optimize quantization vs. quality tradeoffs."

Problem breakdown:
- Current cost reporting is aggregated by model and time-window; customers want per-request mapping and example-level exports.

Suggested immediate actions:
- Add exported CSV sample for 'session -> invoice token mapping' for last 7 days (analytics team).
- Create a how-to: "Using traces + exports to reconcile costs to product events."

Longer term asks:
- Per-route token breakdown in Console alongside latency percentiles; ability to download sample traces.

3) Robust fallback & model routing controls (weight: medium-high) — reported by 12 accounts
Representative verbatims:
- "We need to pin a model variant but allow safe degradation to smaller quantized models when capacity is low."
- "Auto-fallback triggered unexpected quality regressions during a holiday campaign."

Problem breakdown:
- Customers lack fine-grained policy controls for fallback (quality thresholds, deterministic vs. probabilistic).
- No simple staging -> canary -> global rollout primitives that include validation gates.

Suggested immediate actions:
- Ship a set of recommended fallback policies and a console template (canary->rollback) + sample prompts for validation.
- Link to existing rollouts feature but add clearer UX for variant pinning.

Longer term:
- Policy DSL for routing (quality, latency, cost constraints) with audit logs. (Product + Serving runtime).

4) Private deployment onboarding frictions (weight: medium) — reported by 10 accounts, mostly enterprise
Representative verbatims:
- "Our security team expects a deployment checklist and tested VPC template, not a 10-step manual."

Pain points:
- Missing tested IaC modules for common cloud providers.
- Unclear KMS/HSM integration examples and permissions matrix.

Suggested immediate actions:
- Create a VPC quickstart repo (Terraform templates) and a "security checklist" doc. (Owner: private-deployments eng + solutions-eng).
- Offer a 2-week implementation acceleration package via Solutions Eng (pilot offer).

5) Model quality drift monitoring & alerting (weight: medium) — reported by 8 accounts
Representative verbatims:
- "We want alerts when generation quality degrades on our key prompt cohorts — ideally integrated with our SLOs."

Suggested work:
- Out-of-the-box prompt-set evaluation hooks with threshold alerts (tied to Redwood Optimize).

6) SDK ergonomics & examples for advanced features (weight: lower-medium) — reported by 7 accounts
Notes:
- Gaps: examples for streaming with function-calling, KV cache usage patterns, and session affinity.
- Quick win: add 3 reference apps (next-token streaming chat, embedding index + rerank example, cache prefix sample). (Owner: dev-ex)

7) Billing predictability & commitment options (weight: lower) — reported by 6 accounts
Notes:
- Customers request clearer guidance on committed capacity vs. burst billing and predictable reservation pricing for hybrid workloads.

Quantification summary:
- Total accounts sampled: 48
- Reported tail latency issues: 19 (40%)
- Observability asks: 14 (29%)
- Routing/fallback requests: 12 (25%)
- Private deployment friction (enterprise): 10 (21%)

Representative verbatims (direct, anonymized):
- "We're OK with 2–3% quality loss if it halves cost — but only if it's predictable."
- "We need a way to see the exact prompt that caused a 5s tail spike."
- "Console is great but the defaults don't match our production burst profile."

Decisions recommended for leadership:
- Prioritize a cross-team "Burst & FallBack" sprint (4–6 weeks) to deliver: burst-mode toggle, canned fallback policies, and an autoscale tuning playbook. Rationale: directly addresses highest-weight asks and reduces support incidents.
- Fund a "Private deployment quickstart" (templates + 2-week accelerator) as an enablement package to close enterprise deals.

Open questions / risks:
- Need engineering capacity for a new billing tier for burst capacity — potential revenue vs. ops complexity tradeoff.
- Observability exports may increase DB/storage costs; need sizing estimate from analytics infra.

Immediate next steps (owner + ETA):
- CS: Publish this note and workshop with PMs on 2025-07-22 (owner: Leah Martinez).
- Product-hosted-api: Draft UI mock for fallback policy templates by 2025-07-29 (owner: Priya Nair).
- Eng-serving-runtime: Assess feasibility of a 1–2 minute pre-warmed burst pool and estimate cost by 2025-08-12 (owner: Derek Chen).
- Docs: Autoscale tuning doc + checklist by 2025-07-25 (owner: Omar Singh).

Tickets to create (suggested):
- JIRA:ENG-XXXX — "Burst-mode pre-warm pool feasibility"
- JIRA:PROD-YYYY — "Fallback policy templates + Console UX"

Appendix: example account snapshots (anonymized)
- Account A (mid-market, real-time chat): saw 99th pctl jump from 350ms -> 1800ms during marketing push; prefers cheaper fallback model over timeouts.
- Account B (SaaS search): needs per-query token mapping to reconcile billing with internal metrics.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working synthesis; please add further tickets/PRD links inline or suggest other account snapshots to include.
- Requesting product + eng leads to accept or push back on the recommended sprint before 2025-07-22."
